about: Every threshold the factory's judge reads, one file. A threshold is chosen on the record's replays and never tuned live; each carries the n and the window it was read over, or says in terms that it was not read. No default flips under n = 5 runs / 20 tasks: a threshold read under that floor is an `experiment` with its `rollback` named. A Jev `null` at any site routes to that set's rollback in questions.json.
chosen: 2026-09-17, on Fable, from the 2026-09-17 landing replay and a hand read of 62 rows (the stratified fifty plus the twelve the policy would promote)

severity.rule: blocking <=> borne_out >= t1 AND claim_false >= t2 AND actor = implementer AND fixable_in_files >= t3 AND process_only < t4 AND NOT (status = unverified AND status.confidence >= t_status); plan-routed <=> actor = plan at confidence >= t5 AND fixable_in_files < t5_fixable, else today's routeToPlan regex decides; minor otherwise

t1_borne_out.unread: needs `hunks`; no tag carries a pre-fix patch (#1127 reading 3). Set high on judgment: the conjunction is already conservative without it, so a high t1 costs recall, not safety. Adjacent evidence only: #1093's pairwise finding-vs-hunk read, a DIFFERENT question string, AUROC 0.88 at n = 402. THE FIRST THING THE LIVE n = 5 READING MEASURES.

t2_claim_false.window: 1,157 reviewer residuals over 84 runs (evidence + evidence-tinyapp tags through run-183), built 2026-09-16, replayed 2026-09-17
t2_claim_false.basis: hand read of every row promoted
t2_claim_false.detail: at 0.7 the policy promotes 11 of 1,157 graded-minor residuals; a hand read finds 10 right (real defects in FILES: run-104/2, run-115/6, run-146/3, run-166/2, run-166/1, run-170/3, run-88/824, run-90/4; trivial-but-correct run-126/4, run-149/1) and 1 wrong (run-115/1, a worker's `concern:` disclosure of a budget bump — a note, which the factory routes to the note set and never to landing). At 0.8 it promotes 5 and loses five of the real defects. False-block rate at 0.7: 1/1,157 = 0.09%, upper bound (t1 unread)
t2_claim_false.rollback_note: 0.9 promotes nothing on the corpus: the gate goes inert

t3_fixable_in_files.window: 1,157 reviewer residuals over 84 runs (evidence + evidence-tinyapp tags through run-183), built 2026-09-16, replayed 2026-09-17
t3_fixable_in_files.basis: hand read of the promoted set
t3_fixable_in_files.detail: the one plan defect the policy would have promoted at 0.6 (run-127/3, fix = 0.60, a width the constraint forbade conveying) falls out at 0.7; nothing right is lost between 0.6 and 0.7

t4_process_only.window: 1,157 reviewer residuals over 84 runs (evidence + evidence-tinyapp tags through run-183), built 2026-09-16, replayed 2026-09-17
t4_process_only.basis: hand read of the promoted set
t4_process_only.detail: 0.5 would also drop the one false block (proc = 0.50) but drops run-166/1 with it (proc = 0.62, a real defect: a substring grep over a shared log, which the question read as `how the work was produced`). The exam is the first value, so the real defect is kept and the false block accepted

t_status_unverified.window: 1,157 reviewer residuals over 84 runs (evidence + evidence-tinyapp tags through run-183), built 2026-09-16, replayed 2026-09-17
t_status_unverified.basis: label agreement + hand read of 20 rows (strata 2 and 5)
t_status_unverified.detail: Jev answers `unverified` on 1,019 of 1,157 rows (88%): it is a prior, not a skill, so an unconditional `status != unverified` conjunct would demote nearly everything — four real defects in the fifty were suppressed at confidence 0.31–0.63. Against the reviewer's own `unverified:` prefix: conf >= 0.9 gives precision 54%, recall 92%, agreement 91%; hand read of ten no-prefix rows at >= 0.91: 8 right, 2 were verified out-of-FILES observations (`cannot act here` read as `cannot verify`). The promoted set is insensitive to this value across 0.8–0.95

t5_actor_plan.window: 1,157 reviewer residuals over 84 runs (evidence + evidence-tinyapp tags through run-183), built 2026-09-16, replayed 2026-09-17
t5_actor_plan.basis: label recall + hand read of ten no-prefix rows
t5_actor_plan.detail: against the `plan-defect:` prefix at conf >= 0.8: precision 21%, recall 36%. The regex it was to replace reads precision 100% / recall 27% — but its precision is DEFINITIONAL (route_to_plan opens `startswith('plan-defect:')`, so it is a subset of the label), and recall is the only fair axis. Hand read of ten rows Jev routed at >= 0.8 with no prefix: 6 right (the label missed them), 3 were `[structural false-green]` gate rows with no task at all (absent from the live landing path), 1 was an implementer case that fixable_in_files = 0.88 contradicted — hence the guard below. NOT YET EARNED as the regex's replacement; the regex stays the floor
t5_actor_plan.rollback_note: 1.01 = never routes on Jev; the regex alone, #1127's rollback

t5_fixable_guard.window: 1,157 reviewer residuals over 84 runs (evidence + evidence-tinyapp tags through run-183), built 2026-09-16, replayed 2026-09-17
t5_fixable_guard.detail: `plan` is defined as `no edit inside task.files can` resolve it, so a plan route with fixable_in_files >= 0.5 contradicts the answer that produced it. Excludes the one wrong route in the ten read (fix = 0.88); every right route read <= 0.27

k.unread: no corpus has been read at these strings; the prototype forced k. The first real plan with a hard task is the reading

referee.rule: the discovery referee is dispatched when review_difficulty >= 2 (`Careful`), and on the review-difficulty rung alone; doc_or_prose_only is recorded on the row and gates nothing
referee.unread: #1096's jev:tier rows have no n on any tag yet (run-183 predates #1109). The 2026-09-17 first draft read `OR doc_or_prose_only < 0.5`, which would have dispatched a referee on every code task and contradicted the spec's rule that no routine task carries one; caught by the engine plan's gate reader the same day
referee.rollback: the referee dispatched on every task

k_probe.unread: every landing of runs 204-207 (n=12 tasks) carried k: 1, so the selector's line never had two candidates to choose between and could not be calibrated. The pre-registered reading is over the next 5 runs the probe fires on: how often the two candidates differ on exam exit (a real catch) versus only on the claim/coverage tail of the selector's line, and the second implementer's token cost against the modest 126s mean / 335s max already read for implementer dispatch
k_probe.rollback: enabled = false: k is the judge's task reading, which read 1 on every task of runs 204-207

One re-dispatch after this backoff for a worker whose error is a gateway shape and that produced no assistant turn; 0 is no retry. The pre-registered reading per run: infra deaths, retries, retries that succeeded, referees that died twice.

min_elapsed_ms.read: The two-minute floor held over runs 213–220 (n=8): one skipped row on a worker that finished inside it, every worker past it read once.

observed.read: Read with the supervisor cell above: the observed reading fired 29 ticks over runs 213–220, never at 0.8; kept on for the record, gates nothing.

supervisor.read: #1128's pre-registered reading, taken 2026-09-22 over runs 213–220 (n=8 runs, 42 workers, 11 late, 0 errored): the would-have-stopped set at stuck ≥ 0.8 is empty (highest observed score 0.70), and the one tick's score does not separate a late worker from a fast one (run-220's implementers read 0.68/0.69 and finished in 3–4 min; run-215's read 0.57/0.58 and ran 43–45 min). The stop verb stays off; record-only is the default, not an experiment. Rows keep accruing for a cadence reading.
